answer: The horizon report makes public the merge explicitly at each sparrow. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 128 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 220 times the capital for one share. Each collapsed cluster gets one zephyr weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 2 epochs. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
